messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging: High error-rate detected for /v1/generate on cluster 'us-west-gpu'. 5xx ratio 28% over the last 2m. Affected service: serving-runtime. Investigate.

lina: I'm on it. looking at logs now, grabbing recent pod restarts.

raj: I can help — saw spike on metrics too, CPU fine but GPU mem alloc failing. Which node pool is this?

lina: Node pool: gpu-pool-rt-1. Logs show repeated OOM and `CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY`. Pods entering CrashLoopBackOff.

mike: putting preliminary incident summary in #incidents-ops. Suspect autoscaler thrash — HPA/cluster-autoscaler scaling up then down rapidly around pods with large KV caches.

sophia: seeing the same on traces: tail latency up, many requests queued then dropped. Requests routed to smaller model variants sometimes but routing fallback is overloaded.

josh: posting relevant logs:```
2026-03-15T21:12:08Z serving-runtime[model=redwood-v1] ERROR kernel: CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY: failed to allocate 12.3GiB
2026-03-15T21:12:11Z kubelet: Pod "runtime-abc-7f9" failed: OOMKilled
2026-03-15T21:12:15Z cluster-autoscaler: scaleUp: creating node gpu-pool-rt-1-xyz
2026-03-15T21:12:25Z cluster-autoscaler: scaleDown: removing node gpu-pool-rt-1-xyz (unneeded)```

carla: that pattern (scale up then immediate scale down) will terminate pods mid-start, kvcache warmup fails -> repeated restarts. Known issue if eviction/grace period too short.

raj: can we check HPA and autoscaler config? sharing commands:```
kubectl get hpa -n production serving-runtime -o yaml
kubectl get deployment serving-runtime -n production -o yaml
gcloud container clusters describe redwood-us-west --format=json | jq '.autoscaling'
```

lina: HPA target looks fine but minReplicas=0 and scaleDownDelay=30s. cluster-autoscaler scaleDownUnneededTime set to 1m. So scale-downs can happen before pods stabilize.

mike: recommended temporary mitigation: set HPA minReplicas=2, bump scaleDownUnneededTime to 10m, and pin cluster-autoscaler to ignore the gpu-pool until healthy. Also reduce container `resources.requests.gpu` if possible or serve quantized model variant.

sophia: agree. Also enable `podDisruptionBudget` to prevent abrupt scale-downs for critical replicas.

carla: action item list: 1) disable aggressive autoscaler downscales (temporary) 2) increase HPA min 3) rollout a memory-efficient model variant 4) cordon any flappy nodes 5) notify customers.

lina: starting with 1 and 2. applying patch now:```
kubectl patch hpa serving-runtime -n production --type='merge' -p '{"spec":{"minReplicas":2}}'
# update cluster-autoscaler configmap
kubectl -n kube-system patch configmap cluster-autoscaler-config --patch '{"data":{"scaleDownUnneededTime":"10m"}}'
```

deploy-bot: Deploy job started for configmap patch (job id: deploy-20260315-21-14).

mike: while that's rolling, cordoning the worst nodes: `kubectl cordon gpu-node-12 gpu-node-13`. Doing graceful drain where possible.

josh: devex: suggestion to route traffic to smaller-ram model: adding a canary routing rule in the gateway to divert 30% traffic to `redwood-v1-quant` (lower memory).

lina: initiating routing change as second mitigation.

customer-success: FYI sending a proactive status to customers on affected endpoints. I'll say: "temporary brownout and increased errors — engineering intervening; may see degraded throughput for 30–60 minutes." ok?

sophia: yes that message is accurate. add note about retries/backoff to reduce load.

raj: monitoring pod restarts: after patches, restart rate dropped 70%. CrashLoop frequency reduced but still seeing some OOMs on a subset.

mike: looks like a few pods still trying to warm large KV caches and hit mem ceiling. Let's patch runtime to reduce prefetch cache size: `KV_CACHE_MAX_ENTRIES=5000` -> `3000`.

lina: patching deployment env var:```
kubectl set env deployment/serving-runtime -n production KV_CACHE_MAX_ENTRIES=3000
kubectl rollout status deployment/serving-runtime -n production
```

josh: after env change, new pods are stable. No OOMs in last 2 mins, latency back to baseline for the routed traffic.

carla: confirm we left HPA minReplicas=2 and scaleDownUnneededTime=10m? This should avoid future thrash.

lina: confirmed. Also added `stabilizationWindowSeconds: 120` to HPA to smooth scale events.

mike: redeploying autoscaler config to ignore short-lived nodes: set `scaleDownUnreadyTime: 20m` for this GPU pool.

deploy-bot: Config change applied successfully.

customer-success: sent update: "We mitigated a runtime issue causing degraded response rates; we implemented temporary routing and capacity changes. Monitoring continues." Customers acknowledged.

sophia: running post-incident checks: need an RFC to change default autoscaler thresholds for gpu-pools, add unit tests for scale events, and update runbook to include KV cache sizing for large models.

raj: creating follow-up Jira: PRO-1234 "Autoscaler thrash causing serving runtime crashloops" with action items (autoscaler tuning, runbook update, model memory profiling).

lina: handing off to night on-call @mike for monitoring. I'll stay available for 15m then sign off.

mike: taking handoff. Currently error-rate back to <1% and latency stable. Will escalate if anything regresses.

incident-bot: Incident status: Mitigated -> Monitoring. Severity: Sev2. Duration so far: 00:25.

carla: nice work everyone :thumbsup: add retrospective notes and root cause guess: autoscaler scaleDown settings too aggressive + large KV cache warmups -> pods repeatedly killed mid-warmup -> crashloop.

josh: reopening a small note — recommend a longer-term fix: prefer rolling-start policy for pods with large warmups and prefer node-pool-level min nodes for GPU pools.

mike: noted. I'll attach metric graphs and a short timeline to PRO-1234.

lina: signing off on-call. Thanks team.

customer-success: Will follow up with customers tomorrow with RCA and timeline for permanent mitigations.

incident-bot: Incident transitioned to Monitoring at 2026-03-15T21:37:45Z.
